title: India's Top Six IT Firms Shed 24,422 Engineering Roles in One Year
excerpt: Exits of about 92,000 outpaced hiring of 68,000 at TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, Tech Mahindra and LTIMindtree, Xpheno data show, as firms left vacant seats unfilled.
body:
• Combined IT and engineering headcount at TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, Tech Mahindra and LTIMindtree fell 24,422 in a year, from 822,144 in October 2025 to 797,722 in October 2026.
  • The drop is a net figure: about 92,000 people left and about 68,000 were hired, with exits beating hiring in five of the last six months.
  • This is not a layoff count — attrition stayed in the normal 11-15% range, but firms did not refill every vacant seat.
  • For jobseekers: hiring has slowed most for 5-12 year roles in manual testing, maintenance and L1/L2 support, while AI, cloud and cybersecurity demand keeps growing.

India's six largest IT services companies employ 24,422 fewer people in IT and engineering roles than a year ago, as departures outpaced replacement hiring, data from staffing firm Xpheno show.

The combined headcount fell nearly 3%, from 822,144 in October 2025 to 797,722 in October 2026, according to Xpheno figures first reported by The Economic Times. The six firms are Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, Tech Mahindra and LTIMindtree.

A net decline, not a layoff wave

The arithmetic matters. The companies recorded about 92,000 exits over the year, in line with a normal annual attrition rate of 11% to 15%. They hired about 68,000 people in the same functions. The gap between the two numbers is the 24,422 decline.

"Annual attrition has remained at 11-15%, but companies haven't necessarily refilled attrited seats."

— Francis Padamadan, Chief Executive, Xpheno

That distinction separates this trend from a round of mass layoffs. People left at a familiar rate. Companies chose, month after month, not to replace all of them. Exits exceeded hiring in five of the last six months covered by the data.

TeamLease Digital, cited in the same reporting, linked the pattern to workforce optimisation and changing technology requirements, with artificial intelligence reducing the need for routine work in traditional IT roles.

Which roles are under pressure

Xpheno and staffing analysts point to a clear split. Replacement hiring has slowed for mid-level staff with five to 12 years of experience in manual testing, application maintenance, infrastructure support and first- and second-level services, where automation now handles part of the workload.

Demand for specialist roles has moved the other way. Positions in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity and specialist engineering are still growing, creating a mismatch for staff whose experience sits in conventional maintenance work. Firms are also cutting bench strength — staff not assigned to a client project — and pushing internal upskilling in generative AI to protect margins during a period of moderate revenue growth.

Companies are not moving together

Quarterly results complicate a single industry story. In the September quarter, TCS added staff for a third straight quarter, and HCLTech and Tech Mahindra also reported net additions in company-wide results, while Wipro reduced its workforce in the quarter. Those quarterly company totals cover all functions, not only the IT and engineering subset in the Xpheno count, so they do not contradict the year-on-year decline.

For the diaspora, the read-through is direct. Many Indian professionals in the United States, Canada, Britain and the Gulf hold roles or manage teams in exactly the maintenance and support categories where replacement hiring has slowed, and many families in India depend on fresher hiring that large services firms have historically supplied at scale.

What to watch

The next two quarters will show whether the September-quarter additions mark a turn or a pause. If AI, cloud and cybersecurity hiring keeps rising while routine roles keep shrinking, headcount could stabilise even as the mix of jobs changes sharply. If exits continue to beat hiring, the net decline will extend into a second year.
